note: Exemptions are taken verbatim from the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011. An exemption never yields PASS. It yields NOT_APPLICABLE, with the exemption cited.

exemptions.title: Rule 3 — packages above 25 kg / 25 litre and industrial or institutional supplies
exemptions.explanation: Rule 3: 'The provisions of this Chapter shall not apply to,- (a) packages of commodities containing quantity of more than 25 kg or 25 litre excluding cement and fertilizer sold in bags up to 50 kg; and (b) packaged commodities meant for industrial consumers or institutional consumers.'

exemptions.title: Rule 26(a) — packages of ten gram or ten millilitre or less
exemptions.explanation: Rule 26(a): 'Nothing contained in these rules shall apply to any package containing a commodity if— (a) the net weight or measure of the commodity is ten gram or ten millilitre or less, if sold by weight or measure; Provided that the declaration in respect of maximum retail price and net quantity shall be declared on packages containing 10g to 20g or 10ml to 20ml.' The MRP and net-quantity declarations are therefore not exempted for 10-20 g / 10-20 ml packages.

exemptions.title: Rule 26(b) — fast food packed by a restaurant or hotel
exemptions.explanation: Rule 26(b): 'any package containing fast food items packed by restaurant or hotel and the like'.

exemptions.title: Rule 26(d) — agricultural farm produce in packages above 50 kg
exemptions.explanation: Rule 26(d): 'agricultural form produces in packages of above 50 kg.'

exemptions.title: Importer declaration applies only to imported packages
exemptions.explanation: Rule 6(1)(a) requires the name and address of the importer only 'for any imported package'. A domestically manufactured package therefore has no importer declaration to make.

exemptions.title: Retail sale price declarations are directed at retail packages
exemptions.explanation: Rule 6 sits in Chapter II, 'Provisions applicable to packages intended for retail sale'. A wholesale package as defined in rule 2(r) is governed by Chapter III instead.
